report.headline: Projected to take 23.0% of EuroLeague possessions, up from 18.4% in the NBA, but the accompanying true-shooting projection carries no information

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to rise from 18.4% in the 2010-11 NBA season to 23.0% in the 2011-12 EuroLeague, above the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.3%.

risks.text: The true-shooting projection of 57.2% should not be trusted: on held-out data the model's error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the EuroLeague average (4.7% baseline error).
The player was 30 years old in the source season, on the older end for translating production into a new league.
The 95% usage interval (16.2%-29.8%) spans more than 3 standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, leaving wide uncertainty about the actual role size.
The estimate rests on 115 historical NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions, and the players who made this move already sat 0.31 sd below their own league's average, a selection effect built into the model.

strengths.text: In the source NBA season the player posted a true-shooting percentage of 56.7%, 0.51 standard deviations above that year's league average.
Projected EuroLeague usage of 23.0% sits above the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.3%, consistent with an above-average offensive role.
The usage-rate model beats the trivial league-mean baseline on held-out transitions (3.3% MAE vs 4.3%), so this particular projection carries real signal.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 18.6% to 27.5%, and the 95% interval from 16.2% to 29.8% — a span of roughly 3 standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (sd 4.4%). The model can say this is an above-average usage player, not what his exact share will be.
